Definition: straightforward, i.e. (figuratively), equitable, correct, or (abstractly), integrity
BiblicalUsage: Nakoch means straightforward or upright, equitable and correct, and it is used for a case and for a walk. In 2 Samuel 15:3 Absalom tells a man that his matters are good and right, but there is no man deputed of the king to hear him, and in Isaiah 57:2 the one walking in his uprightness shall enter into peace and rest in his bed.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that uprightness is a road, not a pose, because Isaiah's walker enters peace by walking in it; absalom could call a matter good and right and still use it for his own ends.
